title: Hacking of social media accounts - what the FIR should actually state
p1:
Your account was hacked. But is that enough for an FIR?

Many people think writing only “my Instagram/Facebook account was hacked” will start a strong investigation. It usually does not.
p2: The missing detail is often the story of the offence. An FIR should clearly mention what happened: when access was lost, what unauthorized activity occurred, whether passwords or emails were changed, whether messages or posts were made, and what evidence is available.
p3:
A surprising fact: the recovery of an account and the investigation of the offence are different things. A complaint should preserve details like login alerts, suspicious links, screenshots, usernames, phone numbers, email changes, and financial loss if any. These details help investigators trace the person behind the activity.

The practical takeaway: do not describe only the problem; describe the digital trail. The clearer the facts, the stronger the foundation for action.
conclusion: Have you ever faced a hacked social media account? What details do you think most people forget to mention while filing a complaint?
